institutions: Jackson-Madison County General Hospital — 642-bed tertiary care center and flagship of West Tennessee Healthcare; the only tertiary care hospital between Memphis and Nashville, serving a 19-county rural area.
Union University — private Christian university founded in 1823, affiliated with the Tennessee Baptist Convention; 2,718 undergraduate and graduate students on its main Jackson campus.
Lane College — historically Black college founded in 1882 by Bishop Isaac Lane, affiliated with the Christian Methodist Episcopal Church; liberal arts baccalaureate curriculum in east Jackson.
Jackson State Community College — public two-year college whose fall 2025 enrollment topped 4,000, a 16.7% year-over-year increase that led all Tennessee community colleges and public universities.
TCAT Jackson — Tennessee College of Applied Technology campus with 30+ technical programs including industrial maintenance, welding, practical nursing and automotive technology.
highlights: Cypress Grove Nature Park — a 164.8-acre cypress preserve in the Forked Deer River floodplain minutes from downtown, crossed by a 7,136-foot elevated boardwalk, with a 25-acre lake, a 36-foot observation tower and the Aerie Trail Raptor Center; opened October 1985.

Downtown Jackson Arts District — formally approved by Jackson City Council in 2022 and mapped by the city's Public Art Commission; anchored by the Ned R. McWherter West Tennessee Cultural Arts Center, the 1903 Carnegie Center, the Jackson Symphony and the AMP amphitheater at the West Tennessee Farmers Market.

Bemis — a planned cotton-mill village begun in 1900 by the Bemis Brothers Bag Company, now a National Register historic district nominated in 1991; its 1922 Beaux Arts auditorium houses the Bemis Mill Village Museum.

Casey Jones Home & Railroad Museum — the restored home of Illinois Central engineer Casey Jones, with his pocket watch from his last ride, a 35-ton locomotive replica and a Railroads & The Civil War in Tennessee exhibit.
